I built Genos as a connected workspace for chat, tasks, and collaborative notes.
This update lets its agent propose changes to that work.

The constraints matter more than the demo: approval is all-or-nothing; there is
no general undo transaction across entity types; and a preview can become stale
if the underlying project changes before approval. The proposal is generated by
a model, not verified as a good plan. Authorization and input validation still
run when the write executes.

Three concrete flows:

1. Give it a chat thread and ask for a plan. It can propose a milestone, tasks,
   subtasks, assignees, dates, and dependency edges as a task tree.
2. Ask it to reorganize a milestone. It can propose priority/date changes as an
   old→new diff with a reason per row.
3. Ask it to create or refine a note. It previews the full body. On approval it
   writes the persisted note and updates the live Yjs document.

The safety rule is intentionally simple: reads execute; writes pause.

Read tools can search and fetch threads, tasks, notes, and project state. A
mutating tool stores a pending action and ends the response stream. The client
renders a tool-specific approval card. Approve/reject is a separate request using
a one-shot token tied to the stored run and its owner; approval resumes the loop
from the stored steps.

For a multi-item plan, the UI asks once for the whole batch rather than once per
task. That is a UX boundary, not proof of database atomicity. The task-plan
preview is a tree rather than raw JSON; bulk changes use a diff table.

Stack: Django 5 + DRF, React 19, Flask/Socket.IO for messaging, Yjs/Hocuspocus for
notes, OpenSearch for hybrid retrieval, and a tool-calling LLM loop streamed as
NDJSON. Reads and writes are ACL-scoped, and proposals can link back to the
chat/task/note inputs.

Current limitations:

- solo-built MVP; web only;
- plan quality depends on the source discussion and model output;
- approval is whole-batch; there is no partial selection;
- no general undo transaction across every entity yet (version history covers
  notes, but task-plan rollback needs more work);
- collaboration-service failure can prevent an already-open note from seeing an AI
  rewrite live even if the stored copy was updated;
- the approval boundary reduces accidental writes but does not by itself solve
  prompt injection or a user approving a bad proposal;
- moving a team into one workspace is still the biggest adoption cost.

The demo requires no signup: https://genosai.dev. Free plan, no card.

I would especially value criticism of the approval boundary. For a batch write,
would you require partial selection, a freshness check, or transaction-level undo
before trusting it?

---

## Likely questions — concise honest answers

### Why not use MCP across Slack, Notion, and Jira?

That can provide access, but the causal links between a discussion, resulting task,
and superseded note often were never stored. Genos's bet is to capture those links
when work is created. This costs migration/adoption effort; it is not a drop-in
integration.

### Is “one approval” just hiding many dangerous writes?

Yes, it can. The UI renders the complete task tree or diff, but review quality is
still a human factor. Today approval is all-or-nothing. Partial acceptance,
freshness checks, and transaction-level undo are reasonable next steps.

### How do permissions work?

Search filters by team and entity visibility. Tools check authorization against
the requesting user, and the approval token is one-shot and tied to the stored run
and owner. This is an application-level permission system, not a formal
capability-security design.

### What happens if the model hallucinates an ID?

Write tools validate referenced projects/tasks and authorization. The preview
shows titles rather than only opaque IDs. Invalid or inaccessible references fail
instead of being accepted as model output.
